title: Hotloop bench retrospective and smoke notes - Mar 09 2026
body:
Meeting: Hotloop benchmark retrospective + quick smoke runs
Date: 2026-03-09
Attendees: Maya Chen (owner), Ethan Brooks, Priya Nair, Liam O'Connell, Zara Haddad, optional: Samir (observability)
Location: Zoom; notes in Drive; quick playback in bench cluster
Goal: Triage noisy throughput/latency variance observed on hotloop nightly runs (last 3 days). Agree immediate mitigations and experiments to run this week.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Regression window: ~2026-03-06 03:00 UTC onward we see 8-15% p95 latency uplift on 8k sequence LlamaX-13B-quant test in hotloop smoke. Throughput (QPS) varies with microbursts and KV-cache miss rate appears correlated.
- Hypothesis A: recent scheduler change (PR #1427) to conservative batching backoff increases small-request latency under mixed workload.
- Hypothesis B: KV-cache eviction jitter due to new multi-tenant patch path created more prefix misses on warmup.
- Short-term mitigation: pin scheduler to previous algo in dedicated canary, force KV-cache TTL extension for warmup period, and widen autoscaling headroom for 2h smoke window.

Observed metrics (quick grab from bench-run-2026-03-08.log):
- Experiment: mixed-seq-8k/1k ratio 1:3, model LlamaX-13B-quant, batch target 16
- Baseline (2026-03-05): p50=58ms, p95=121ms, p99=245ms, QPS=320
- Post-change (2026-03-08): p50=62ms, p95=137ms, p99=312ms, QPS fluctuates 280-340 (spiky)
- KV-cache hit rate baseline: 92% -> observed 84% on regression runs
- Warmup period anomalies: first 30s of run see 30% lower throughput then recover; correlates with prefix-db refreshes in logs

Trace snippets / notable logs: (copied lines)
- "sched: backoff applied, target_batch 8 -> 4 due to latency pressure" (2026-03-06 03:12:11)
- "kvcache: eviction triggered, tenant=shared-2, freed=112 entries, ttl=300s" (2026-03-06 03:12:13)
- "warmup: prefix-refresh request=18 total=26, awaiting remote sync" (2026-03-06 03:12:14)

Hypotheses and quick experiments to run this week (priority order):
1) Revert scheduler backoff change in a canary + run hotloop smoke 3x to confirm latency fall-back. Owner: Ethan. Deadline: 2026-03-11.
   - Run: bench-run --profile hotloop-mixed --target-batch 16 --runs 3 --model LlamaX-13B-quant --tag revert-sched
   - Success criteria: p95 returns within 3% of baseline and p99 drops by >10%
2) Force longer KV-cache TTL for shared tenants on canary nodes to test if eviction is main driver. Owner: Priya. Deadline: 2026-03-12.
   - Config: kvcache.default_ttl=900 -> bench cluster only
   - Measure: hit-rate improvement and correlation with p95
3) Replay workload with fixed microburst generator (deterministic inter-arrival) to rule out synthetic load variability. Owner: Liam. Deadline: 2026-03-11.
4) Increase early warmup retries for prefix DB sync to avoid initial miss storm (hotfix candidate). Owner: Zara. Deadline: 2026-03-10 (if safe)

Notes to self (informal):
- We saw one long-tail event that lines up with CONN-201 spike in infra network logs (Samir to confirm). If network hiccups cause repeated prefix fetches that could amplify load on remote store.
- Look into adding a short-lived local prefetcher for common prefixes in hotloop harness. Prototype suggestion: prefetch top-50 prefixes for first 60s.
- Reproduction tips: use bench image builder v2.8.1 (contains latest kernel + profiling) and ensure bench ingest uses same tokenization seed as nightly.

Immediate action items (owners + status):
- Ethan: roll canary with scheduler revert, run smoke cases, post results in thread (#bench-notes). Status: TODO
- Priya: patch KV-cache TTL on canary, instrument hit-rate per tenant, upload histograms. Status: TODO
- Liam: synthetic microburst generator script updated (bench/microburst/v2) and add deterministic seed option. Status: in_progress
- Zara: draft prefix-retry hotfix and quick safety checklist. Status: TODO
- Maya (me): compile final run artifacts and create one consolidated dashboard snapshot by EOD next Friday. Status: TODO

Open questions:
- Can we reproduce the same p99 amplification with a single-tenant dedicated run? If not, multi-tenancy interactions likely.
- Does the scheduler change interact with batch-splitting heuristics and cause more small-batch flushes? Need to inspect telemetry on 'batch-split' counter.
- Should we change KV-cache eviction policy to LRU windowed vs global LRU? Risk = memory growth on tail tenants.

Longer-term ideas (parking lot):
- Adaptive prefetcher based on sequence prefix popularity heatmap (requires prefix analytics pipeline).
- Scheduler A/B test framework for gradual backoff policy rollouts (tune at config-level without code revert).
- Better bootstrapping for bench harness to avoid first-1m noise (warmup forks, prefetch)

References / artifacts used:
- bench artifacts: s3://redwood-bench/hotloop/2026-03-08/run-423.tar.gz
- PR under suspicion: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1427 (scheduler conservative backoff)
- KV-cache change: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kv-cache/commit/7a1c3b2
- Jira tickets: JIRA-RT-3981 (regression triage), JIRA-OPS-7112 (infra network spike)

Next check-in: quick async updates in #bench-notes, formal sync Thu 2026-03-11 09:30 PT to review canary results.

Appendix: quick run commands and env clarifications
- bench-run CLI (examples):
  bench-run --cluster bench-canary --profile hotloop-mixed --model LlamaX-13B-quant --runs 3 --target-batch 16 --out /tmp/run-423 --log-level debug
- Env: bench-canary nodes run kernel 6.4.21, gpu driver 535.86, runtime image redwood/bench:v2.8.1
- Metric collection: push to prometheus bench-canary endpoint, export snapshot via bench-exporter -> s3

End of notes.
